walkthroughs.body_html:
Lagos boomed due to:

• Oil discovery in the Niger Delta (1950s)
• Pull factors — jobs, education, healthcare
• Push factors — rural poverty, conflict

In 1960 Lagos had 300,000; today 15 million+.

Lagos offers:

• Banking and finance hub
• Nollywood film industry
• Telecoms and tech growth
• A huge informal sector (~70% of jobs)

Each new factory job creates a multiplier effect.

Rapid growth brings problems:

• Slums like Makoko (built on stilts over lagoon)
• Sanitation — limited sewage systems
• Traffic congestion
• Water supply issues

Around 60% live in informal settlements.

mcqs.q: Roughly what % of Lagos jobs are in the informal sector?
Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary effects of an earthquake?
options: Primary effects are the worst effects and secondary effects are minor.
Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
Primary effects occur immediately as a direct result of shaking (building collapse, deaths); secondary effects follow afterwards (fires, tsunamis, disease, homelessness).
Because the government forces them to move to cities.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Primary effects happen first and secondary effects happen the next day.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
Climate change only happens in summer.
